findings: main.tex:288-291 (C-31, proved): the printed theorem is false for every choice of linear parts. An affine toroidal family is encoded as the image of a model (EGF.AffineToroidalModel, EGF.affineToroidalFamily: a non-empty parameter type, translations as parameters, a softmax head and a scalar head). For d >= 1 and det A_i = ±1, every model whose two heads ignore the state (softmax weights and outflow density constant in x, translations arbitrary and varying with the parameter) gives a family that is not epsilon-universal, a fortiori not universal (EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_constantHeads): each member leaves lambda invariant and has F_out = c lambda, so F_out pi = F_out, and from 2*1_{E^c} lambda to 2*1_E lambda (lambda(E) = 1/2) the defect is at least the total variation, proved >= 1 (it is 2) (EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_inflow_eq). Instances: the constant model with free translations, Θ = (Fin p -> T^d) x R>=0 (l.288 read literally), and the constant model at any fixed translations b (EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow). So no satisfiable assumption on the Phi_i alone makes Theorem 3.5 true (at d = 1 the unsatisfiable assumption of l.820 makes it vacuously true, EGF.universalityToriPrinted_one). The printed statement as a Prop over models, EGF.UniversalityToriPrinted d (l.820's condition required of the moves at every parameter), is refuted as soon as some moves meet l.820 (EGF.not_universalityToriPrinted, by the constant model at those translations: a non-empty family, every member with these very moves); that some moves meet l.820 needs a non-amenable group of linear parts and is not proved here. Disclosed: EGF.UniversalityToriPrinted admits det = ±1 (GL_d(Z)) where the paper has SL_d(Z), a strengthening of this refuted Prop (immaterial: moves meeting l.820 exist in SL_d(Z) for d >= 2, not in Lean, and EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow covers SL_d(Z) unconditionally); a one-point model refutes it as well, so the informative statements are EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_constantHeads and EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow.

main.tex:291 corrected (C-28 + C-29 + C-31, proved): EGF.universality_tori_of_ergodic: if the group generated by the moves (det A_i = ±1) acts ergodically on (T^d, lambda) and the family is rich (C-31, EGF.IsRichToroidalModel), it is epsilon-universal; any family, in particular the family of any rich model; no spectral gap, no aperiodicity, no inverse-stability, no named Prop. The richness is met by a model (EGF.l2ToroidalModel, EGF.isRichToroidalModel_l2ToroidalModel), and for its family ergodicity of the group is also necessary (EGF.universality_tori_iff, through EGF.isKernelErgodic_torusUniformKernel_iff: the uniform kernel is ergodic iff the group is).

main.tex:818-820 (C-28 route, proved): from Bekka-Guivarc'h, a group violating (ii) has a spectral gap; a spectral gap of the action makes the action ergodic (EGF.ergodic_of_hasSpectralGap: 1_A - lambda(A) would be an invariant unit vector of L2_0), and ergodicity suffices (EGF.universality_tori, from hBG); the inverse-stability of l.820 is not needed. On l.818's claim that the kernel with alpha^i = 1/p 'has spectral gap': in l.273's sense (the spectrum of the transfer operator bounded away from 1 on L2_0) it follows from the action's gap with no aperiodicity (the operator is an average of unitaries, a contraction, so 1 in its spectrum would give almost invariant vectors for every generator, hence for the group; not formalized, and not used). Bekka-Guivarc'h's criterion for a spectral radius < 1 (which summable L2-mixing needs) assumes the generating measure aperiodic, which the minimal four moves are not (C-28 (a)). The two-sided gap nevertheless holds there, and for every group of affine maps violating (ii): a point of modulus 1 in the spectrum (an approximate eigenvalue) would give a character whose kernel has almost invariant vectors, hence satisfies (ii), hence so does the group (for the minimal four moves at b = 0, also directly: L2_0(T^2) is a permutation representation of SL_2(Z) with stabilizers isomorphic to Z, so it is weakly contained in the regular representation and Kesten gives norm < 1). Not formalized and not used. So the paper's route l.818 -> l.273 -> Theorem 3.4 does not fail at its spectral-gap step there for d >= 2 (with l.273 in C-30's two-sided form); Theorem 3.4 still needs C-31's richness, and at d = 1 the route fails (C-28 (b)); ergodicity is all this file needs.

main.tex:293 and main.tex:821 (C-28 (b), proved): on T^1 every group of affine maps satisfies (ii) (W = 0, projection in {±1}, finite hence amenable and virtually abelian: EGF.bgConditionII_dim_one). So the technical assumption of l.820 is never met at d = 1, the printed theorem under that reading is vacuously true there (EGF.universalityToriPrinted_one), 'in any dimension' (l.149, l.293) fails for this route at d = 1 (SL_1(Z) is trivial: its 'two generators and their inverse' give translations only), and l.821's 'SL(d,Z) contains a free group with two generators' is false at d = 1. On T^1 universality still holds from one translation of infinite order through ergodicity (EGF.universality_tori_of_ergodic; the instance is T-egf-tori-minimal (planned)).
main.tex:283-286 vs Bekka-Guivarc'h: the paper's Aff(T^d) has linear parts in SL_d(Z), Bekka-Guivarc'h's in GL_d(Z) = Aut(T^d); every theorem here assumes det = ±1, so it covers the paper's family.
questions: 'mild technical assumptions' (main.tex:291) are not stated in the theorem; reading taken: the condition of main.tex:820 (as C-28 records), required of the moves at every parameter of the model (EGF.UniversalityToriPrinted; the refuting constant model has the same moves at every parameter, so it also refutes the reading 'at some parameter'). The conclusion is read in the epsilon-form (weaker than def:universal_family, so the refutation is the stronger).

'affine toroidal family' (main.tex:288): the model is unspecified. Reading taken (EGF.AffineToroidalModel): a non-empty parameter type; per parameter, translations that are a function of the parameter (free, as in EGF.constToroidalModel; tied in inverse pairs; or fixed, as in EGF.constToroidalModelAt), positive measurable weights summing to 1 (a softmax head) and a real outflow density, clipped at 0, of finite mass (a scalar head); the family is the image of the parameter type. With all translations free over the torus, l.820 cannot hold at every parameter (for d >= 1) (inverse-stability fails at some translations, unless every A_i = -I, whose linear parts satisfy (ii)), so in that reading the printed theorem is vacuous rather than false, and the every-parameter reading is refuted through models that tie the translations. Continuity of the family (l.288) is not encoded; the class is larger, and the refuting models are continuous. The positive theorems do not depend on this reading (they hold for any family with the richness of C-31).

labels.label: theo:spectral_gap_tori

hypotheses.paper: H a countable subgroup of Aff(T^d) (main.tex:812)
hypotheses.note: H : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (UnitAddTorus (Fin d))), Countable H, every element affine x -> Ax + b with det A = ±1 (IsTorusAffine; Bekka-Guivarc'h's Aff(T) = GL_d(Z) ⋉ T); p_a(H) = linearParts H, well defined by EGF.torusAffine_inj

hypotheses.paper: (i) the action of H on T(^d) does not have a spectral gap (main.tex:814)
hypotheses.note: ¬ HasSpectralGap volume H: the Koopman representation U(h)xi = xi ∘ h⁻¹ on the complex L2_0(T^d) has almost invariant vectors, in Bekka-Guivarc'h's sequence form (arXiv:1106.2623v1 p. 1: unit xi_n in L2_0 with ||U(h)xi_n - xi_n|| -> 0 for all h in H)

hypotheses.paper: (ii) a non-trivial H-invariant factor torus T-bar with the projection on Aut(T-bar) amenable (main.tex:815)
hypotheses.note: BGConditionII (linearParts H): a Q-subspace W ≠ Q^d of Q^d invariant under every linear part (T-bar = T^d / (W/(W ∩ Z^d)), the rational subspace W ⊗ R), and the subgroup of GL_Q(Q^d/W) formed by the projections u_A ([v] -> [Av]) amenable as a discrete group (a left-invariant finitely additive probability on all subsets). Aut(T-bar) = GL((Z^d+W)/W) embeds in GL_Q(Q^d/W), so the image groups are isomorphic. Every A has a unique projection (EGF.exists_factorProjection, EGF.factorProjection_unique) and the subgroup generated is exactly the projection of p_a(H) (EGF.mem_closure_factorProjection_iff)

hypotheses.paper: (iii) of Bekka-Guivarc'h (virtually abelian; not printed in main.tex)
hypotheses.note: the named Prop carries all three items: (i) <-> (ii) and (ii) <-> (iii); IsVirtuallyAbelian = an abelian subgroup of finite index
the Prop is stated for every d; at d = 0 it is proved (EGF.bekkaGuivarchTheorem5_zero)

findings: Cited theorem (DEC-141): stated as the named Prop EGF.BekkaGuivarchTheorem5 d, never an axiom, a hypothesis of EGF.universality_tori only; the printed (i) <-> (ii) is EGF.spectral_gap_tori, proved from it. Non-vacuity: for d >= 1 the trivial group H = ⊥ meets its hypotheses (countable, affine) and satisfies (i), (ii), (iii) (EGF.bekkaGuivarch_witness_bot: it fixes the set {x | x_0 in [-1/4, 1/4]} of volume 1/2, so it is not ergodic and has no spectral gap; W = 0, trivial projection); at d = 0 the Prop holds outright (EGF.bekkaGuivarchTheorem5_zero). Not in Lean: any H with a spectral gap for d >= 1 (that requires the non-amenability Bekka-Guivarc'h's theorem converts), so the (i)-false side is witnessed only at d = 0, and universality_tori has no instance for d >= 1 (at d = 0 it holds degenerately: bekkaGuivarchTheorem5_zero, and ¬ BGConditionII holds for every L since Q^0 has no proper subspace).

Source read: arXiv:1106.2623v1 (Bekka-Guivarc'h), fetched 2026-11-21 by this closer (the planner's /tmp copy was not present): §1 p. 1 (definition of spectral gap, sequence form), §1 (factor tori, Theorem 1), §2 Theorem 5 (items (i)-(iii)). questions: Real or complex L2: Bekka-Guivarc'h's Koopman representation is unitary, read on the complex L2_0 (ξ : X -> ℂ); the real form is equivalent (real and imaginary parts of an almost invariant vector), not formalized.
Almost invariant vectors in the sequence form (Bekka-Guivarc'h p. 1), equivalent to the (finite set, epsilon) form for countable H (Theorem 5's hypothesis); the equivalence is not formalized.

corrections.notes: Tori half, proved sorry-free (standard axioms only). The corrected Theorem 3.5's ergodicity clause: EGF.universality_tori_of_ergodic (the group generated by the moves acts ergodically, plus C-31's richness, gives epsilon-universality), and its 'this holds when that group has no non-trivial invariant factor torus on which its linear part projects to an amenable group (Theorem 5)': EGF.universality_tori, from the named Prop EGF.BekkaGuivarchTheorem5 d through EGF.ergodic_of_hasSpectralGap (a spectral gap of the group makes it ergodic). Gap (a) of C-28 is bypassed: by C-29 only ergodicity is needed (no spectral gap of the kernel at all). For the record: Bekka-Guivarc'h's criterion for a spectral radius < 1 (which summable L2-mixing needs) assumes the generating measure aperiodic, which the minimal four moves are not (C-28 (a)); the two-sided gap nevertheless holds there, and for every group of affine maps violating (ii): a point of modulus 1 in the spectrum (an approximate eigenvalue) would give a character whose kernel has almost invariant vectors, hence satisfies (ii), hence so does the group (at b = 0 also by Kesten, L2_0(T^2) being weakly contained in the regular representation of SL_2(Z)). Not formalized and not used. So the paper's route l.818 -> l.273 -> Theorem 3.4 does not fail at its spectral-gap step there for d >= 2 (with l.273 in C-30's two-sided form); Theorem 3.4 still needs C-31's richness, and at d = 1 the route fails (C-28 (b)). For the master (outside this closer's paths): C-30's registered 'needs the generating measure aperiodic before l.273 applies' and C-28 (a) carry a milder form of the same over-statement (AUDIT-2). The uniform kernel is ergodic iff the group is (EGF.isKernelErgodic_torusUniformKernel_iff), with no aperiodicity and no inverse-stability; ergodicity is necessary too (EGF.universality_tori_iff). Gap (b) is proved: on T^1 condition (ii) always holds (EGF.bgConditionII_dim_one), so the printed theorem is vacuous at d = 1 (EGF.universalityToriPrinted_one). Not here: the hyperbolic-element / cat-map route and the T^1 translation instance (T-egf-tori-minimal, planned), and that some group violates (ii) for d >= 2 (non-amenability).

Tori half, proved sorry-free. The added hypothesis is carried as IsRichToroidalModel A b F (the uniform policy of the moves with outflows f lambda for every f of a set dense in the non-negative cone of L2(lambda)) by EGF.universality_tori_of_ergodic and EGF.universality_tori, for any family, in particular the family of a model; it is met by the L2 model (EGF.isRichToroidalModel_l2ToroidalModel). Fix round 1 (AUDIT-1 major): an affine toroidal family is now the image of a model, EGF.affineToroidalFamily A M = range (M.flow A), M : EGF.AffineToroidalModel d p with a non-empty parameter type, translations as parameters, a softmax head and a scalar head; the membership predicate IsAffineToroidalFamily, which the empty family satisfied, is removed. The refutation: for d >= 1 and det = ±1, a model whose heads ignore the state is never epsilon-universal (EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_constantHeads), instantiated by the constant model with free translations and at any fixed translations (EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow). The printed statement as a Prop over models, EGF.UniversalityToriPrinted (l.820's condition at every parameter), is refuted whenever its condition is satisfiable (EGF.not_universalityToriPrinted, by the constant model at those translations). A one-point model refutes it as well (the printed statement conditions only the moves), so this refutation certifies only that some model fails; the informative statements are EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_of_constantHeads and EGF.not_isUniversalFamilyEps_constOutflow. Disclosed readings: UniversalityToriPrinted admits GL_d(Z) moves (the paper SL_d(Z)), a strengthening of a refuted Prop, immaterial; with all translations free, l.820 cannot hold at every parameter (for d >= 1), so the printed theorem is then vacuous and the refutation ties the translations; continuity (l.288) is not encoded, the refuting models are continuous. Conditional on the existence of moves meeting l.820, which is not proved in Lean.

The tori instance of C-29's remark 'for Theorems 3.5-3.6 ergodicity of the group generated by the moves suffices': EGF.universality_tori_of_ergodic applies EGF.universality_of_ergodic_family (strict, not redefined) to the uniform kernel; EGF.universality_tori_iff adds necessity for the uniform-policy family. Offered as additional anchors; C-29's own anchors are unchanged.

kb_proposals: Haar measure preservation on UnitAddTorus without a Jacobian: Measure.isAddHaarMeasure_map_of_isFiniteMeasure (continuous surjective hom) + Measure.isAddHaarMeasure_eq_of_isProbabilityMeasure (EGF.measurePreserving_torusLin); translations by measurePreserving_add_right. Mathlib's IsProbabilityMeasure (volume : Measure UnitAddCircle) is local to Analysis/Fourier/AddCircleMulti (whose mFourier/L2 lemmas use haarAddCircle through a local MeasureSpace, not the global volume); EGF.isProbabilityMeasure_volume_unitAddCircle provides it globally (move it to a shared module if T-egf-tori-minimal (planned) also needs it).

Group-action notions for cited theorems (amenable, virtually abelian, almost invariant vectors, IsGroupErgodic) live in EGFScaffold.TorusFamilies, stated for any MeasurableSpace X and H : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm X): the sphere target should import them, not redefine them. IsGroupErgodic is Mathlib's MeasureTheory.ErgodicSMul (Dynamics/Ergodic/Action/Basic.lean) without the invariance of the measure; for measure-preserving H they agree (EGF.isGroupErgodic_iff_ergodicSMul; ErgodicSMul's parent SMulInvariantMeasure is an instance argument of its constructor: build it with haveI first). Finite groups give cheap witnesses (EGF.isAmenableGroup_of_finite via Set.ncard).

Countability of a finitely generated subgroup: FreeGroup.closure_eq_range + inferInstanceAs (Countable (Quot _)) for the FreeGroup + (Set.countable_range _).to_subtype (EGF.countable_torusAffineGroup).

Pitfalls at this pin: Equiv.Perm.apply_inv_self does not exist, use h.apply_symm_apply (h⁻¹ x is h.symm x); push_neg is deprecated, use push Not; a `set` variable blocks rw of its body (state `show <body> = _` first); integral_unique produces Unique's `default`, not syntactically Inhabited's: finish with congr 1 + Subsingleton.elim; on a quotient, ext a LinearEquiv and take q = W.mkQ v by W.mkQ_surjective.

A paper's 'parameterized family' is the image of a model, never a membership predicate: Set.range (M.flow A) over a structure with a non-empty parameter type (EGF.AffineToroidalModel). A predicate on members is satisfied by the empty family and makes any 'every such family is universal' Prop refutable for nothing (AUDIT-1 of T-egf-families).
